quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #4
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: When should drivers yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk?

options.text: Only if the pedestrians wave first.
Only if the pedestrians are not texting.
Always.

questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle at a crosswalk to let pedestrians cross. You can only go when your lane is completely clear.

questions.question: You see a pedestrian crossing your lane with no crosswalk. You should:

options.text: Make eye contact and then pass the pedestrian.
Slow down as you pass the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.
questions.explanation: You must yield to pedestrians at intersections, even if there is no crosswalk. Let them cross safely.

questions.question: When driving on gravel or dirt roads:

options.text: Your tires grip better than on pavement.
Your tires have less grip, so you must slow down.
You can see better than on pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your tires have less grip, so you must slow down.
questions.explanation: Tires grip loose gravel and dirt less than they grip pavement. Slow down on these roads. It takes longer to stop and it is easier to skid when turning.

questions.question: What can you do to reduce road rage?

options.text: Always signal before changing lanes.
Talk on your cell phone while driving.
Use your horn frequently.

questions.explanation: To prevent road rage, follow all traffic laws and signs. Always signal when changing lanes.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and prepare to stop if cars are coming.
Come to a full stop, then go when it is safe.
Go through carefully without always stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a full stop, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: An octagonal sign means stop. Stop completely at the stop line. If there is no line, stop before the crosswalk. If there is no crosswalk, stop where you can see traffic.

questions.question: The maximum posted speed limit should only be driven:

options.text: At night.
During the day.
In perfect conditions.

questions.explanation: The posted speed limit is the fastest speed you can legally drive in ideal conditions. Drive at the same speed as traffic around you, up to this limit. All drivers must drive at a safe speed.

questions.question: You can identify an aggressive driver by:

options.text: Sudden and unsafe lane changes.
The number of passengers in their car.
Their slow driving.

questions.explanation: Watch other drivers for aggressive behavior like unsafe lane changes. Do not challenge them. The safest action is to stay away from them.

questions.question: What does this yellow warning sign mean?

options.text: You are near a school or school crosswalk.
Slow down, drive safely, and watch for children.
Both A and B.

questions.explanation: This sign is placed near schools to warn drivers to slow down, drive safely, and watch for children.

questions.question: Night driving is harder because:

options.text: The speed limit increases at night.
There are fewer cars on the road.
It is hard to judge distance and speed in the dark.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is hard to judge distance and speed in the dark.
questions.explanation: Night driving creates problems because you cannot see as far. It is hard to judge the distance to other vehicles and their speeds. You can only see as far as your headlights.

questions.question: When driving in work zones, you should:

options.text: Follow the driver in front of you closely.
Pass the driver in front as soon as you can.
Keep a safe distance and do not tailgate.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a safe distance and do not tailgate.
questions.explanation: In work zones, keep a safe distance from barriers, trucks, equipment, workers, and other vehicles. Stay back further than normal and do not tailgate.

questions.question: What is a dangerous habit when driving in work zones?

options.text: Following another vehicle too closely
Not watching carefully for workers and equipment
Both of the above

questions.explanation: In a work zone, slow down and keep distance from other vehicles. Watch carefully for workers and machines.

questions.question: Driving under the influence of drugs carries what penalty?

options.text: The same penalty as driving under the influence of alcohol
A smaller penalty than driving under the influence of alcohol
No penalty at all

questions.correctAnswerText: The same penalty as driving under the influence of alcohol
questions.explanation: Driving under the influence of any drug — including legal medications — has the same penalty as driving under the influence of alcohol.

questions.question: After drinking three beers in one hour, how long does it take for all the alcohol to leave your bloodstream?

options.text: One hour
Two hours
Three hours

questions.explanation: It takes about three hours for your body to process three drinks.

questions.question: Before stopping at a traffic signal or sign, you should:

options.text: Press the accelerator hard
Check your mirrors for traffic around you
Set the parking brake

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors for traffic around you
questions.explanation: When stopping, first check your mirrors for traffic around you. Release the accelerator smoothly, then press the brake pedal with steady pressure for a smooth stop.

questions.question: What driving skills are affected by alcohol and drugs?

options.text: Alertness
Coordination
Both of the above

questions.explanation: Alcohol and drugs harm many driving skills. They slow your reaction time, reduce coordination, lower alertness, and hurt your ability to focus.

questions.question: When taking medicine, you should:

options.text: Ask your doctor about side effects before driving
Have someone follow you home
Keep your window open and drive slower

questions.correctAnswerText: Ask your doctor about side effects before driving
questions.explanation: Both prescription and over-the-counter medicines can affect your driving. Always ask your doctor or pharmacist how a medicine will affect your driving ability. This is especially important for tranquilizers and sedatives.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: One-way traffic
Intersection ahead
Traffic merging from the right

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to hazards ahead. This sign warns you that traffic will merge from the right.

questions.question: If you are getting tired while driving, you should:

options.text: Stop and rest or let another driver take over
Drink something with caffeine
Open a window

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest or let another driver take over
questions.explanation: Stop every hour or so on long trips to rest. Share driving with another person so you can both stay alert.

questions.question: What is a crosswalk?

options.text: Another name for a four-way intersection
An area for road construction workers
An area where pedestrians can cross the road

questions.correctAnswerText: An area where pedestrians can cross the road
questions.explanation: Crosswalks are marked with white lines to show where pedestrians cross. Some crosswalks are unmarked, but they still show where pedestrians have the right to cross.

questions.question: As daylight fades, you should use your:

options.text: Parking lights
Low beam headlights
Emergency flashers

questions.explanation: Turn on your low beams as daylight fades so others can see you. Use high beams only when driving in an open area with no other drivers.

questions.question: When must you stop your vehicle?

options.text: When a police officer tells you to stop.
When there is a red traffic light.
Both of the above.

questions.explanation: You must stop at a red traffic light. You must also obey a police officer's orders to stop, even if traffic signs or signals say something different.

questions.question: A school bus has flashing lights and its signal arm is extended. What should you do?

options.text: Stop.
Drive at 15 mph if no children are visible.
Drive at normal speed, but watch for children.

questions.explanation: You must stop completely when a school bus has flashing lights and an extended signal arm. Stay stopped until the arm is pulled back and the bus moves. This rule applies whether you are behind the bus or coming from the opposite direction.

questions.question: What is distracted driving?

options.text: Anything that causes you to swerve while driving.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that makes you focus more on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving means anything that takes your eyes, hands, or mind off the road. It is the leading cause of traffic accidents. Any distraction can cause you to miss important signs and sounds needed to avoid crashes.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the road mean?

options.text: Slow down.
A traffic light is ahead.
Do not pass.

questions.explanation: A solid yellow line means you cannot pass other vehicles. When a solid yellow line is next to a broken yellow line, drivers on the solid yellow side cannot pass. When both lines are solid, no one can pass from either direction.

questions.question: Your reaction time becomes slower after:

options.text: Drinking alcohol.
Getting sleep.
Working hard.

questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reflexes and reaction time. It reduces your eyesight and makes you less alert. As you drink more alcohol, your judgment gets worse and your driving skills decline. You will have trouble judging distances, speeds, and other vehicles' movements.

questions.question: What does this yellow pennant-shaped sign mean?

options.text: Right turns only.
Right turns are allowed.
No passing zone.

questions.explanation: Yellow pennant-shaped signs warn drivers of a no passing zone ahead.

questions.question: Tailgating (driving too close to the car in front of you):

options.text: Can make other drivers angry and frustrated.
Cannot result in a traffic ticket.
Prevents other cars from cutting in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can make other drivers angry and frustrated.
questions.explanation: Tailgating is dangerous behavior that can lead to aggressive driving. You can be ticketed for unsafe driving.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Always give way to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Oncoming traffic and pedestrians must give way to you.
Never give way to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always give way to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: When turning left, you must yield to cars coming toward you. You must always yield to pedestrians.

questions.question: On a two-lane road, if you drive faster than other cars and pass many of them, you will:

options.text: Reach your destination faster and more safely.
Increase your risk of a crash.
Help reduce traffic congestion.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your risk of a crash.
questions.explanation: Avoid passing other vehicles on two-lane roads. Each time you pass a car, your chance of a crash increases.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: An intersection is ahead.
A steep hill is ahead.
The road curves ahead.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns of a steep hill ahead. Slow down and be ready to shift to a lower gear to control your speed and protect your brakes.
